title: Large Trades and Intraday Futures Price Behavior (indexed as: The Price Impact of Institutional Trades on S&P 500 Index Futures)
one_line: In CME futures, large customer BUYS have bigger permanent (information) price impact than large sells, while sells have bigger temporary (liquidity) impact that reverses; the asymmetry flips with market state (sells matter more in bear markets).

findings.statement: Permanent impact: buys > sells; temporary impact: sells > buys.
Bear markets: large sells carry more information; bull markets: buys.

why.pattern: Liquidity-driven selling partly reverses; information-driven buying persists.

reported_results.headline: In CME futures, large customer BUYS have bigger permanent (information) price impact than large sells, while sells have bigger temporary (liquidity) impact that reverses; the asymmetry flips with market state (sells matter more in bear markets).

tradable_edge: No strategy (needs trade-level customer flags). Context for forced_selling_flush_fade_es: liquidity selling reverses, but less so in bear regimes.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
